# Axis-B RIGOROUS findings — the credibility-hardened test (supersedes the headline)

*Generated by `axisB_rigorous.py` (8 seeds). Crisis (GFC 2008 in test) and calm
(2014–2020) windows. All nonlinear models share the SAME information set and NEST the
strong linear baseline (HAR-X), so a quantum win would require nonlinearity beyond the
linear span of identical inputs. Diebold–Mariano uses a Newey–West HAC variance; the
family of CHIMERA-vs-control tests is Holm-adjusted. Figure: `figures/fig_axisB_rigorous.png`.*

## Why this supersedes the first Axis-B result

The first Axis-B run reported "CHIMERA beats HAR (DM p=0.004) at n=10." Our own
adversarial review found this conflated **richer inputs** with **quantum processing**:
plain HAR has only 3 features, while CHIMERA was fed leverage / downside-semivariance /
jump measures. The decisive control — **HAR-X**, the *same* extra features used **linearly**
(no reservoir) — was missing. We added it, plus a **true recurrent ESN** and an **RFF/RBF
kernel** control, HAC-DM, 8 seeds, two windows, and Holm correction.

## Results (8-seed ensembles; RMSE of log-RV, lower=better)

**Crisis 2007–2012** (plain HAR: RMSE 0.6290, MZ 0.559):

| n | HAR-X | ESN | RFF | CHIMERA | CHIMERA vs HAR-X (HAC p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8  | **0.6255** | 0.6386 | 0.6302 | 0.6379 | +2.63, p=0.009 (worse) |
| 10 | 0.6034 | **0.5996** | 0.6047 | 0.6074 | +1.17, p=0.240 |
| 12 | **0.5906** | 0.6023 | 0.5964 | 0.6031 | +1.97, p=0.050 (worse) |

**Calm 2014–2020** (plain HAR: RMSE 0.6454, MZ 0.205):

| n | HAR-X | ESN | RFF | CHIMERA | CHIMERA vs HAR-X (HAC p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | **0.6244** | 0.6445 | 0.6264 | 0.6291 | +0.96, p=0.335 |

**Multiple-comparison control (Holm across all 12 CHIMERA-vs-control tests): nothing is
significant at 0.05 in either direction** (smallest Holm p = 0.103, which is CHIMERA
*worse* than HAR-X at n=8).

## Honest conclusions

1. **The dominant lever is the encoded information, not the reservoir.** HAR-X — leverage,
   downside-semivariance and jump measures used *linearly* — is the best or co-best model in
   almost every cell, and crushes plain HAR (e.g. crisis n=12: 0.5906 vs 0.6290). The
   accuracy gain comes from *which features you encode*, a known econometric result
   (SHAR/HARQ), not from quantum (or any) nonlinear reservoir.
2. **No quantum advantage at simulable scale.** CHIMERA never beats HAR-X (it is slightly
   worse; raw-significant at n=8 and n=12) and is statistically indistinguishable from the
   classical ESN/RFF after Holm correction (one raw-significant loss to RFF at crisis n=8,
   p=0.049, also in the "worse" direction). The **95% Model Confidence Set retains all four
   models in both windows** (crisis n=10: CHIMERA p=0.117, HAR-X/ESN/RFF p=1.000; calm n=10:
   ESN p=0.159, others p=1.000) — a statistical tie on the decisive family. **H0 is REFUTED**,
   exactly as pre-registered — we committed to reporting this.
3. **What honestly survives for the quantum reservoir:** it is *competitive* (within ≈0.8–2.1%
   RMSE of the best at every n, i.e. ≤0.013 log-RV RMSE points), with **lower per-seed
   dispersion than the recurrent ESN in 3 of 4 window/n cells** (s.d., e.g. n=12: 0.009 vs
   0.015; the exception is crisis n=10), and it *does* beat the recurrent ESN on the calm
   window (raw p=0.018; n.s. after Holm). Together with the measured kernel distinctness
   (`kernel_analysis`) and full-rank entanglement (`tensor_backend`), these are genuine,
   quantum-specific *properties* — but they are **necessary, not sufficient** for a
   forecasting advantage, which we do not observe here.

## Bottom line

A pre-registered, adversarially-controlled study finds that at ≤12–16 simulable qubits the
quantum reservoir provides **no statistically significant forecasting advantage** over strong
classical baselines on S&P 500 realized volatility; the decisive factor is informed feature
encoding. We report this negative honestly. Whether the quantum reservoir's distinct,
classically-hard feature map converts into an advantage *beyond* the classical-simulation
frontier remains the open question — now framed without overclaiming a win that does not exist.
